subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion & reserved throughput SLA amendment (Velotech)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@velotech.io>, Elena Su <elena.su@velotech.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal proposal: Dedicated pool expansion + throughput SLA amendment

Oliver / Elena —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Based on your usage growth and the capacity and latency goals you shared, attached is a clean addendum that incorporates the dedicated pool expansion and a reserved throughput SLO. High-level summary: 

- Add 8x A100 (40GB) GPUs to your existing dedicated pool (total reserved capacity increases by 8 GPUs).
- Reserved throughput guarantee: 50,000 tokens/sec sustained measured as a 1-hour rolling window across the reserved pool.
- P95 generation latency target for standard requests (<= 220ms) under normal operating conditions.
- Credits: if sustained throughput < 50k tokens/sec for more than two non-overlapping 1-hour windows in a month, Velotech receives a 10% monthly credit on Dedicated fees for that month; additional remediation path described in section 4.
- Term: renewal extends existing contract by 12 months from 2026-04-01 with the upgraded pool. Pricing summary is in the attached addendum.

Please review and let me know whether you want us to: (a) proceed to countersign via DocuSign; (b) schedule a short ops call to align measurement definitions (metrics pipeline, sampling); or (c) request alternative SLA thresholds.

Attachments: Velotech_Dedicated_Addendum_v1.pdf (PDF) — redlines + SLO language; throughput_baseline_q1.csv — usage/throughput baseline for Feb.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@velotech.io>

Date: 2026-03-01T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: Dedicated pool expansion + throughput SLA amendment

Rachel —

Thanks for the quick turn. This looks promising and exactly what we discussed. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we loop procurement: 

1) Measurement: is the 50k tokens/sec baseline measured after prefix caching and KV-cache hits, or is it at the inference runtime (post-cache)? We want guarantees to apply to what our application sees (i.e., post-prefetch).
2) Credits math: can we scale credits for multi-month regressions (e.g., consecutive months underperforming)?
3) Maintenance windows: what planned maintenance windows will take the pool down and how will they be excluded from SLO calculations?

Would like to get procurement in this week. Happy to do a 30-min call with Marcus/Monica to align.

—Oliver
Head of Platform, Velotech

[Note: forwarding the addendum to procurement for intake.]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: Dedicated pool expansion + throughput SLA amendment

Rachel / Marcus —

Looping you in to prep on the measurement and SLO details. Quick notes as I reviewed the addendum: 

- Measurement point: we should define "observed throughput" as tokens/sec measured at the Redwood control plane's ingress after prefix/KV cache hits (i.e., what is delivered to the serving runtime). That aligns with what they see as generated tokens. But if Velotech insists on end-to-end application-level measurement we need to agree on a shared telemetry export (we can provide a signed metrics stream).
- Credits: suggest tiered credits: 10% for first qualifying month, 20% for the second consecutive qualifying month, and 30% for a third consecutive month; this gives a remediation incentive.
- Maintenance: propose excluding scheduled maintenance windows up to 8 hours/month (with 48-hour notice). Emergency maintenance will be studied case-by-case and excluded if we provide postmortem.
- SLA enforcement: require a five-business-day remediation period to investigate before any credit is applied.

I can join the alignment call; Marcus, can you confirm whether the runtime already emits the per-pool tokens/sec metric we reference?

Monica
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_addendum_clause_draft.docx (DOCX, 52 KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal: Dedicated pool expansion + throughput SLA amendment

Monica / Rachel —

We already export a per-pool metric named redwood.pool.tokens_per_sec (1s resolution) and a derived rolling window series. We can (and should) publish a signed, read-only metrics endpoint for Velotech that contains the same series. Technical clarifications: 

- "Sustained 50k tokens/sec": we measure as an average across the reserved pool (sum of tokens generated by all GPUs in the pool) in a 1-hour rolling window. Cache hits are included in the generated token count — that'll be consistent with what their application consumes because caching happens at the runtime layer.
- Maintenance exclusion: we can emit maintenance markers; scheduled windows with 48-hour notice will be excluded automatically. Emergency maintenance will be flagged and postmortemed; exclusions require an ops report within 5 business days.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms measured on generation API calls for 'standard' route. Leader routes (large-system calls) are out of scope.

I will prep the metrics endpoint and a short doc describing exact metric names for the call.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

[Inline: Marcus attached a short metrics spec in the internal doc repository — link sent separately.]
